items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: All the Jarreau horn parts were — I don’t think we played a note before eleven maybe... And on the Jarreau record we had already been booked during the day.

ctx.x: Yeah he had a great thing going on with those rhythm guitars and a certain kind of effect on them was really distinctive. I understand he liked to start his studio sessions like at midnight or something.

Yeah. All the Jarreau horn parts were — I don’t think we played a note before eleven maybe, and we would finish at six or seven in the morning. And on the Jarreau record we had already been booked during the day. You know the movie calls come out a month © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

ahead of time and so you know we’re booked on other sessions from nine o’clock in the morning ‘til six at night, you know playing on these, whatever TV movies and everything. And then we’d go to the Jarreau session and start at eleven and go ‘til six or seven. Literally go home, take a shower, go to the nine o’clock or ten o’clock session. And we did that for a week for the Jarreau stuff. And on the fifth day, the Friday of that week, we had a nine o’clock call with Bill Conti for the 1984 Olympic music. And…
